subject: mathematics
question_text: In a △ABC, if a = 13, b = 14 and c = 15, then show that R = 65/8, r = 4, r₁ = 21/2, r₂ = 12 and r₃ = 14.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.44 — LAQ chapter 6 Properties of Triangles, answer 32, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: TS 17 · AP 15,16,17,19 — five printed tags, the most-asked LAQ in this unit. The reverse of answers 31.x: the SIDES are given and the five radii are wanted. The book calls it "Roc'king... Q! Superrrr...Q!" and its split is printed in full. THE MARK SPLIT IS PRINTED in that book's margin as [1 Mark] against each of seven working lines — a fully sourced 1+1+1+1+1+1+1, and the only printed split in this chapter. The book's chapter header carries ★★★ and reads '7 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section C runs Q18-Q24 at 7 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q24 is the Properties of Triangles slot. Together with Q17 (SAQ) this unit holds TWO slots — one of only two units to do so, Matrices being the other. Re-cut to the 8-mark Section-C form of the 2026-27 pattern (TGBIE model paper w.e.f. 2026-27): the extra mark goes to the "Find Δ by Heron" step.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

steps.label: Find s
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the book prints [1 Mark] for it. Everything downstream needs s, so it is computed and displayed on its own line.
steps.memory_tip: 2s = a + b + c, so s = 21. Everything downstream needs s — give it its own line.

recall.must_convey: That 2s = a + b + c = 42, so s = 21.
accept: two s is the sum of the sides which is forty two so s is twenty one
the semi perimeter is twenty one
add the sides and halve to get s
a plus b plus c forty two, s twenty one
find the semi perimeter first

steps.why: s is the semi-perimeter — HALF the sum. Forgetting to halve is the single commonest slip, and it corrupts every value after it.

steps.label: Find Δ by Heron
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Heron's formula. Group the factors into perfect squares — 3²×4²×7² — rather than multiplying out to 7056.
steps.memory_tip: Group the factors into perfect squares, 3² × 4² × 7², rather than multiplying out to 7056.

accept: use herons formula, root of s into s minus a s minus b s minus c which is eighty four
the area is eighty four
group the factors into squares to get three times four times seven
heron formula tho delta eighty four vasthundi
the area comes to eighty four

steps.why: Every one of the five radii below is a fraction with Δ on top. Getting Δ right is worth more than any single one of them.
common_mistakes: Multiplying to 7056 and then struggling with the root.

steps.label: Find R
steps.margin_note: Third mark. R = abc/(4Δ) — the circumradius. The 65/8 does not simplify further.
steps.memory_tip: R = abc/(4Δ), the circumradius. 65/8 does not simplify further.

accept: R is a b c over four delta which is sixty five over eight
the circumradius is sixty five eighths
use R equals abc by four delta
R equals abc by four delta, sixty five by eight
the circumradius comes to sixty five over eight

steps.why: R is the only one of the five that uses the product of the sides rather than Δ over something. It is worth memorising separately for that reason.

steps.label: Find r
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. r = Δ/s — the in-radius, and the simplest of the five.
steps.memory_tip: r = Δ/s, the in-radius and the simplest of the five.

accept: r is delta over s which is eighty four over twenty one equals four
the in radius is four
use r equals delta by s
r equals delta by s, four
the in radius comes to four

steps.why: r = Δ/s is the definition that all the others are built around — r₁ is the same with s−a in place of s.

steps.label: Find r₁
steps.margin_note: Fifth mark. r₁ = Δ/(s−a) — the same shape as r, with s−a underneath.
steps.memory_tip: r₁ = Δ/(s − a) — same shape as r, with s − a underneath.

accept: r one is delta over s minus a which is eighty four over eight equals twenty one halves
r one is twenty one over two
use delta over s minus a
r one equals twenty one by two
the first ex radius is twenty one halves

steps.why: The three ex-radii differ only in which side is subtracted. Once one is written the other two are mechanical.

steps.label: Find r₂
steps.margin_note: Sixth mark. Same again with s−b.
steps.memory_tip: Same again with s − b: r₂ = Δ/(s − b).

accept: r two is delta over s minus b which is eighty four over seven equals twelve
r two is twelve
use delta over s minus b
r two equals twelve
the second ex radius is twelve

steps.why: Each ex-radius is larger when its side is larger, since s − side is then smaller. r₂ > r₁ here because b > a.

steps.label: Find r₃ and conclude
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Same with s−c, then state all five together as the question asked.
steps.memory_tip: Same with s − c, then state all FIVE together as the question asked.

recall.must_convey: That r₃ = Δ/(s−c) = 14, and all five values are stated together.
accept: r three is delta over s minus c which is fourteen, and then state all five values
r three is fourteen and the five answers are stated
the last ex radius is fourteen
r three equals fourteen, anni five values rasta
give all five results together

steps.why: The question named five quantities, so the last line must name all five. An examiner reading only the final line should see the whole answer.
common_mistakes: Reporting only r₃ at the end.
